plans.note: Sec 21 is the operative cap; check mutuality, cap quantum vs Fees, exclusion of indirect damages, and whether the 'Excluded Claims' definition in Sec 1 carves out IP indemnity, confidentiality, data breach and willful misconduct. Cross-check Sec 20 indemnity for any cap interaction.

Sec 20 should contain Vendor IP infringement and misconduct indemnities; confirm defense/control mechanics and that any Customer-side indemnity is narrow (Customer Data / misuse only). Sec 14 and 15 may cross-reference IP and data-breach indemnity.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline; scan Customer Responsibilities, Compliance and General for any covenant limiting the businesses we operate or competing products we buy or build.
Check the scope/structure clause and Order Form mechanics for sole-source or 'all requirements' language before concluding absence.
Direction rule: only flag if the pricing or general provisions oblige Customer to extend best terms to Vendor; an MFN running in our favour is acceptable and should not be redlined.

Non-solicits typically sit in General or alongside Confidentiality; if present, verify it binds both parties, is limited to ~12 months and personnel actually engaged, with a general-advertising carve-out.

Sec 9 governs termination rights; confirm Customer may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice without early-termination or wind-down penalties (check Sec 10 effects and Sec 7 for termination fees), and that Vendor lacks a symmetrical mid-term walk-away.
Sec 8 sets term and auto-renewal; assess the non-renewal notice window length and whether renewal pricing uplift is capped (uncapped uplift is a rationale note unless it defeats the fallback).
Verify governing law is NY, DE, CA or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign-seat arbitration; note escalation/mediation steps without flagging them separately.

Sec 24 covers assignment and change of control; confirm Customer may assign to Affiliates and successors without consent and that Vendor cannot terminate or reprice on our change of control (cross-check Sec 9 termination triggers).

Direction rule: confirm Customer owns Deliverables paid for and all Customer Data (Sec 14/15), and that no clause assigns our IP, data or feedback-derived rights to Vendor beyond a narrow service-delivery licence in Sec 13.
Sec 13 is the grant; check it extends to Affiliates and contractors acting for us, is non-revocable during the term (suspension rights aside) and matches the Vendor Technology definition in Sec 1.

Sec 22 audits of Customer usage: test frequency (no more than annual), advance written notice, business-hours/off-site-where-possible conduct, and Vendor bearing its own cost absent material underpayment. Sec 23 may hold records-retention support obligations.

Direction rule: service credits or SLA remedies running to us in Sec 3 are welcome and should not be flagged; look in Sec 7 and Sec 9 for late-payment penalties or liquidated damages payable by Customer.

Sec 19 warranties: check duration of the performance/Deliverable warranty, that the remedy is re-performance or refund rather than illusory, and whether disclaimers gut it. Sec 6 acceptance and Sec 3 service levels are related but should not be double-flagged.
Sec 18 exists; confirm coverage lines and limits (commercial general liability, professional/E&O, cyber) and evidence-of-coverage/notice obligations given Vendor hosts Customer Data.
Check the fees and Order Form provisions for committed volumes, take-or-pay or non-reducible minimums on renewal; acceptable only with a termination or reduction path.

Sec 11 is the transition and data-return clause; verify assistance period length, availability regardless of termination cause, export format for Customer Data, and deletion certification (cross-check Sec 10 effects and Sec 15 data provisions).
